extracted.intended_audience: general 19th-century Protestant/readership and critics of Catholic institutions (readers of the Maria Monk controversy)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used in the pamphlet to assess the truthfulness of Maria Monk's 'Awful Disclosures' — including tests of probability, eyewitness corroboration, archival documentation, legal/affidavit procedure, and willingness to submit to inspection or trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question of Probability
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of probabilities may be tested by another fact; and that is the full, unshaken conviction, and the serious declaration of many persons who have lived in Canada, that Maria Monk's allegations... are precisely the counterpart of their ordinary character, spirit, and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improbability to outsiders is not decisive; improbabilities should be judged by those acquainted with the subject (Popery/monastic systems). If persons familiar with the system find the account probable, that counts strongly for credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration by residents/former residents
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many persons now residing in the city of New York, who long dwelt in Montreal and Quebec... and such of them as are known, with scarcely a dissenting voice, proclaim the same facts which every traveller... learns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent testimony from people who lived in the region and have first-hand acquaintance with local institutions is treated as strong corroboration; testimony from emigrant residents in another city (e.g., New York) is specifically cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archival / historical documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The inordinate licentiousness ... is demonstrated to be of long standing by the archives of that Province, as may be seen in Smith's History of Canada; year 1733, Chapter 5, p. 194.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published government/historical records to show historical precedent for alleged abuses; archival citations are offered to rebut claims that the events are impossible or novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony of former clergy/insiders
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Samuel B. Smith... interrogated Maria Monk respecting those affairs... he plainly averred that it was manifest she could not have known the things which she communicated to him unless she had been a nun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements by former priests or persons with direct institutional experience (insiders) that affirm the author's detailed knowledge are treated as highly probative of authenticity and firsthand exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and variety of witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred other persons probably can be adduced... Fifty other persons from that province, now residing in New York, likewise attest the truth of the 'Disclosures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad, cross-class attestation (many witnesses of different social standing and places) is emphasized as strengthening the account; geographic spread of attestations (Montreal, Quebec, New York) is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct physical inspection of the nunnery
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit me to go through the Hotel Dieu Nunnery... and if they do not find my description true, then discard me as an impostor... whoever shall explore the Hotel Dieu Nunnery... will find unquestionable evidence that the descriptions... were furnished by one familiar with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An on-site, impartial inspection of the institution is proposed as a decisive test; physical features that 'no mason or carpenter can make and effectually conceal' are singled out as objective evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to face judicial examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring me before a court of justice--there I am willing to meet Lartigue, Dufresne, Phelan, Bonin, and Richards, and their wicked companions... before ten thousand men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readiness to submit to confrontational legal proceedings or public examination (naming alleged perpetrators, offering to be tried) is presented as a credibility-enhancing action; the challenger invites legal scrutiny as proof of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal affidavit procedure for nuns/minors
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws required the affidavit of a nun or minor to be taken before a superior magistrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural legal requirements (which magistrate may take an affidavit, language/form of affidavit) can invalidate improperly taken affidavits; a magistrate signing an English document he cannot read may render it legally insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence, intimidation, and official obstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: I am perfectly satisfied that this was owing to the influence of the priests to prevent my accusations against them from been made public... it was found impossible to induce the magistrates to do any thing in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When formal legal remedies or investigations are absent, consider whether influence, intimidation, threats of excommunication, or other pressure explain that absence rather than falsity of the charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of objectors and weight of their denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the publication... much solicitude has been felt... It is most remarkable, that the incredulity is confined almost exclusively to Protestants, or at least, to those who pretend not to be Papists... The only persons who attempt to hint even a suspicion of the truth of the secrets divulged... are editors of Newspapers... men profoundly ignorant of Popery and Jesuitism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess denials according to the deniers' proximity to the matter; denials from uninformed commentators or hostile editors are treated as weaker than silence or indirect tactics by implicated parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with known regional practices and patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Nunneries in those cities are notorious places of resort for the Roman Priests for habitual and unrestrained licentiousness... many Infants and Nuns... are annually murdered and buried within their precincts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allegations align with commonly reported regional patterns (anecdotes, local reputation, repeated stories at ports/wharfs), that consistency is presented as supporting evidence—though the pamphlet uses dramatic language and sweeping claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed procedural/ceremonial knowledge as proof of firsthand status
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Smith questioned Maria Monk expressly respecting those affairs, customs and ceremonies, which appertain only to nunneries... and, after having minutely examined her, he plainly averred that it was manifest she could not have known the things which she communicated to him unless she had been a nun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge of secret rituals, ceremonies, or internal procedures that only insiders know is treated as a key indicator that the narrator was indeed within the institution described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted Catholics' testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. ----, a widow lady now in New York, who formerly was a Papist in Montreal, and was recently converted to Christianity, solemnly avers, that the Priest Richards himself, conducted her from the Seminary through the subterraneous passage to the nunnery, and describes the whole exactly in accordance with the statement of Maria Monk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony from former adherents or converts who have broken with the institution is used as persuasive corroboration, especially when their accounts align with the principal narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governmental/toleration evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The British government, by the treaty made upon the surrender of that province to them, guarantied to the Papal Ecclesiastics, both male and female, their prior exemptions and special immunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating that authorities historically tolerated or protected the institutions in question explains the persistence of alleged abuses and rebuts the objection that 'government would not permit such wickedness.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspicious conduct in official examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The two legal gentlemen... began a mock examination of me... the person behind me took no active part... I was informed that the examination had been satisfactory, and that I might go. I then returned home; but no further step was taken by the Attorney General, and he refused, as I understood, to return my affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the integrity of official interviews/examinations: staged or partial examinations, concealed participants, retention or non-return of affidavits, and lack of follow-up are indicators that institutional bias or protection may have influenced outcomes.
